Benchmarking: demultiplexing with genotyping vs HTO

2026-08-03

Runs: pilot 260423_VH01624_453_222HWMYNX (where the parameter sweep was done), then `260522, 260528, 260717 through the pipeline.

Status: settled. positive.quantile = 0.99 was adopted and is what the Nextflow pipeline runs for every sample.

Analysis finished: 2026-07-28 - the most recent of the 46 figures shown below.

Report generated: 2026-08-03 by 07.demux_benchmark_report.Rmd, from the outputs of steps 01-06 in this folder.

Samples are pooled several to a GEM well, so every cell has to be assigned back to a donor. Two independent methods are available: hashtag oligos (HTO), which are added at the bench, and genotype demultiplexing from the RNA itself via cellsnp-lite and vireo. This report compares them.

For full report, download demux_benchmark_report.html in the attachment and open in a browser.

Code used - attached and in the github repository: https://github.com/nbartonicek/surface_proteome_dev/tree/main/lab_archives/Benchmarking-demultiplexing_with_genotyping_vs_HTO

Aim

Decide which demultiplexing method to carry into the pipeline, and on what setting:

  • do HTO hashing and genotype demultiplexing recover the same donors
  • which assigns more cells as confident singlets, and which calls more doublets
  • what positive.quantile threshold should HTODemux use
  • does the method still work for a donor that was never hashed

Conclusions

  • genotyping with cellSNP/vireo outperforms HTO hashing, and is the method the pipeline now relies on for donor assignment
  • HTO is still worth running: it is what names the donors, since vireo only produces anonymous donor0…donorN labels that have to be matched back to sample identity
  • positive.quantile = 0.99 was adopted after the sweep and is what every pipeline run uses; the pilot’s original 0.80 is too permissive
  • the unhashed-donor case works after the fix in nextflow/bin/process_cellsnp_hto.R, verified against LK3’s real output rather than a reimplementation

1. How the two methods are produced

HTO comes from CITE-seq-Count on the hashtag library (step 01), whitelisted to the emptyDrops barcodes, then HTODemux. Genotype demultiplexing (step 02) runs cellsnp-lite over the same barcode list against the Cell Ranger BAM, then vireo with N_DONORS=4. Step 03 joins the two and produces everything below.

The important asymmetry: vireo output is anonymous. It returns donor0, donor1 … with no idea which is which. HTO is what supplies the mapping from genotype cluster to sample name, which is why both are run even though genotyping is the better classifier. That mapping is saved as vireo_to_hto_sample_name_map_positive_quantile_0.99.csv.

5. The unhashed donor

Not every donor in a pool carries a hashtag. Step 06 checks that case: it runs the production script nextflow/bin/process_cellsnp_hto.R with exactly the arguments the pipeline module would pass for LK3-GEX, against that run’s already-completed cellSNP/vireo and HTO output. Running the real script rather than a reimplementation is the point - it exercises the code that ships.

The trial output lives in scripts/TRIAL_output_unhashed_donor_demux/, deliberately outside nextflow/, following the convention that trial and diagnostic scripts never sit inside the pipeline directory.

6. What was run, in order

Step Script What it does
01 01.hto_count.sbatch CITE-seq-Count on the HTO library, whitelisted to emptyDrops barcodes.
02 02.cellSNP_vireo.sh cellsnp-lite pileup over the same barcodes, then vireo with N_DONORS=4.
03 03.process_cellSNP_HTO.R Joins vireo onto the object, cross-tabulates against HTO, writes the sweep.
04 04.QC_HTO_ADT_only.R QC restricted to the HTO and ADT modalities.
05 05.QC_HTO_comparison.R Compares HTO and ADT behaviour between the LK1 and LK2 runs.
06 06.test_unhashed_donor_demux.sh Verifies the unhashed-donor fix against LK3’s real output.
07 07.demux_benchmark_report.Rmd This report.

The biotin-specific part of step 05 was later split into scripts/6b1.biotin_ADT_comparison.R, which belongs to the biotin report rather than here.

9. Caveats

  1. The sweep exists only for the pilot run. From LK2 onwards only the 0.99 outputs were generated, so the comparison across thresholds cannot be redone from saved files for the later runs without re-running step 03.
  2. results/demux_comparison/ has no entry for LK1-resequenced or LK3. Those runs were demultiplexed through the pipeline, so their comparison lives under results_nf/<run>/.
  3. Vireo’s donor labels are anonymous; any statement tying a genotype cluster to a sample name depends on the HTO mapping in vireo_to_hto_sample_name_map_positive_quantile_0.99.csv.
